classification.difficultyReason: Interpret a seasonal graph, compare its shape with trigonometric graphs and identify its range and period.

content.prompt: The graph shows the average monthly temperature of a city over 2 years, starting in Jan.

spec.description: Monthly connected data trace retaining the source's irregularities. Horizontal grid intervals represent two months; vertical intervals represent 5 degrees Celsius. Source magenta series maps to house purple and cyan grid to house light blue.
spec.mathematics: Two approximately annual temperature cycles, with minima near 10 degrees Celsius and a maximum near 24 degrees Celsius. The trace contains 24 monthly readings; the final labelled January tick is beyond the last reading.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied data, axes, labels and grid remain visible in the student edition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Would you expect this city to be in the Northern or Southern Hemisphere?

answer.short: Southern Hemisphere; temperatures are high in January.
answer.worked: January is near the warmest part of the cycle, consistent with summer in the Southern Hemisphere.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Which trigonometric graph does this resemble? A cosine or sine graph?

answer.worked: It resembles a cosine graph because it starts near a maximum and then decreases.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If temperatures of a city in the Northern hemisphere were graphed, what graph would you expect, and why?

answer.short: An inverted cosine graph, because temperatures would be low in January.
answer.worked: January is in winter in the Northern Hemisphere, so the graph would start near a minimum. This resembles an inverted cosine curve, shifted vertically to the temperature range.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is the difference between the highest and lowest values?

answer.worked:
The highest temperature is about $24^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and the lowest is about $10^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
$$24-10=14^\circ\mathrm{C}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: What is the period of this graph?

answer.worked: The time between successive winter minima is about 12 months, so the period is 1 year.
